bug_semantics: WebAuthn login is replayable because the per-login challenge never becomes server-side state. prepareForLogin() generates a challenge and mutates the stored-key JSON by reference, and authenticate() is supposed to compare the assertion against that stored challenge then burn it. Both login-prepare and login callers treat the mutated string as a local, never calling User::setWebAuthnKeys(), so the next login re-reads keys that register() persisted with only {key,id} and no challenge. authenticate() then fails open: if (!isset($key->challenge)) the anti-replay throw is skipped, and the only other challenge check compares attacker-supplied originalChallenge against attacker-supplied clientData. A captured successful assertion therefore authenticates indefinitely without the hardware key.
flaw_origin: The missing persist and fail-open replay guard were first written together when WebAuthn/Passkeys were added on 2024-09-11. phpMyFAQ/Auth/AuthWebAuthn.php was adapted from the davidearl/webauthn PHP helper, whose prepareForLogin docblock already told callers to store the revised key blob 'to avoid replay attacks', but Frontend/WebAuthnController::prepareLogin() returned prepareForLogin($webAuthnKeys) without setWebAuthnKeys(), login() likewise discarded authenticate()'s burned challenge, and authenticate() used isset($key->challenge) && mismatch. Registration did persist keys, so the omission is login-specific. Later refactors (route/format/move of the API controller) carried those lines; they did not first write them.

Vendor advisory mechanism: prepareForLogin stamps challenge onto key objects; neither login-prepare handler calls setWebAuthnKeys; register() stores only key+id; authenticate() skips replay when $key->challenge is unset; $info->originalChallenge vs clientData is same-request attacker-controlled. Suggested fix is persist after prepareForLogin and after authenticate, plus fail-closed missing challenge.

BIC 05c3e6d48a981118e06d0d26c242f213ec33bf4c (2024-09-11, 'feat: added experimental support for WebAuthn / Passkeys') first added phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Auth/AuthWebAuthn.php and phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Controller/Frontend/WebAuthnController.php. Single parent 05ba616ecc6abaa289b686ca95edc5fb9edcc16a; not a merge. git grep prepareForLogin and git ls-tree | rg -i webauthn on the parent are empty.

At BIC, Frontend/WebAuthnController.php:135-137 is ` $webAuthnKeys = $this->user->getWebAuthnKeys(); return $this->json($this->authWebAuthn->prepareForLogin($webAuthnKeys), Response::HTTP_OK); ` with no setWebAuthnKeys. login() at :153-155 calls authenticate() without persisting the burned challenge. register() at :112 does call setWebAuthnKeys, so persist was known and omitted only on login.

At BIC AuthWebAuthn.php:219-220 docblock on prepareForLogin: 'You should store the revised $userWebAuthn back to your database after calling this function (to avoid replay attacks)'. prepareForLogin :242 writes $webauthn[$idx]->challenge = $challengeB64. register() :192-194 builds stored objects with only $publicKey->key and $publicKey->id. authenticate() :296-298 is fail-open `if (isset($key->challenge) && $key->challenge != $info->response->clientData->challenge)`. :288-293 compares $info->originalChallenge to clientData (both request-supplied).
